analysis.title: The CEO Macro Briefing Book 4Q26: After the hike, ahead of the vote
key_insights: UBS CIO classifies the current regime as reflation: strong growth with elevated prices, driven by Middle East oil supply pressure and AI demand. Oil is above USD 100 per barrel.

Coincident GDP trackers point to 3Q26 growth close to 5% q/q annualized, far above trend, despite higher prices and interest rates. CEO optimism is at its highest in years alongside a rising ISM manufacturing PMI.
AI capex is forecast to exceed USD 1tr next year (CIO global forecast: 488bn in 2025 to 900bn in 2026E to 1,200bn in 2027E) and is an increasingly important contributor to real GDP growth.
Inflation relief is not coming from abroad. The import price index ex-petroleum is elevated from supply chain stress, and AI demand is pushing up computer parts prices.

UBS expects the Fed to hike two more times, in December 2026 and March 2027, before a dovish pivot. The CIO forecast of one cut by the end of 2027 is out of consensus and rests on slower 2027 growth from waning fiscal support and tighter financial conditions.

The latest inflation report surprised to the upside, reinforcing concerns that disinflation progress has stalled. Rates have risen across the curve after one hike, with market pricing running ahead of the Fed.
Consumer spending is driven by balance sheets, not income. Household net worth is at an all-time high relative to disposable income because of the stock market, while wage growth lags spending.

Consumer sentiment (University of Michigan) is at record lows because of prices and sluggish wages, with lower-income households hit hardest. Nominal retail sales are running at the fastest pace in years, and debt service ratios have fallen despite higher rates. Spending is increasingly dominated by higher-income households.
Labor demand cooled in 3Q as more firms adopted AI tools. Payrolls are treading water, unemployment is near historical lows at 4.2%, layoff announcements are few, and wage growth is slowing.
AI adoption is rising in both public and private data. Average monthly spend on AI tools per median employee rose from $5.6 in 12/2025 to $15.7 in 9/2026, roughly 3x.
Financing conditions are modestly tighter on higher rates, though banks report easier loan standards and NFIB loan availability holds up. The financing composite is softer after the Iran war.

There are signs of distress across the AI stack. Tech spread widening is generally idiosyncratic, but credit markets are scrutinizing some hyperscalers and non-accruals in private credit have surged, though not yet to alarming levels.

Prediction markets (Kalshi) put the odds of a Democratic House and Senate (Blue Wave) at about 50% and a Democratic House with Republican Senate at about 40%. Historically the S&P 500 rallies in the weeks after a midterm election.

UBS sees a very high legislative bar to meaningfully slow AI investment under either a Split Congress or Blue Wave outcome. A divided Congress raises shutdown and debt-limit risk, while a Blue Wave would likely mean wider deficits and less fiscal drag.

UBS raised its 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth forecast to 25%. In 3Q earnings season (10% of S&P 500 market cap reported), the share of EPS beats is above average but has eased, and the magnitude of beats is slightly below average.
Valuation compression from higher rates has already occurred, as the S&P 500 12-month forward P/E moved with the 10-year yield. UBS suggests the adjustment may already be done.

Dealmaking slowed in 3Q on higher rates and uncertainty. Mega deals dried up while whale deals above $10bn rose. PE exits are improving, some mega IPOs were postponed, and AI took 81% of VC deal value.

Market dashboard as of 20 October 2026: S&P 500 7713 (+12.7% YTD), IT sector +22.6% YTD, Energy +52.0% YTD, oil 98.0 (+77.3% YTD), gold 4124 (-4.5% YTD), USD 102 (+3.5% YTD), EUR 1.12 (-4.3% YTD). US small cap +11.7% YTD.

sector_views.rationale: AI capex above USD 1tr next year and rising AI adoption support growth. IT is up 22.6% YTD, though credit markets are scrutinizing some hyperscalers.
Energy is up 52.0% YTD on oil above USD 100 per barrel from Middle East tensions. The report gives no explicit rating.

earnings_insights: UBS raised its 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth forecast to 25% (CIO forecast, 2026E).

3Q26 earnings season: 10% of S&P 500 market cap had reported as of 20 October 2026. The percentage of companies beating EPS estimates is above average but lower than the last two quarters, and the size of beats is slightly below average.
Valuations have compressed because of a more hawkish Fed.

risk_factors: Fed tightening further, with hikes in December and March, could slow growth in 2027.
Higher rates compress valuations and tighten financial conditions.
Stress in the AI stack: credit scrutiny of hyperscalers and surging private credit non-accruals.
Sluggish wage growth and record-low consumer confidence, with lower-income households squeezed by prices.
Oil above USD 100 and AI-driven demand keep inflation above target.
Divided Congress raises shutdown and debt-limit risk.
IPO backlog and high rates keep liquidity locked up in private markets.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong growth, near 5% 3Q tracking, robust AI capex and resilient consumers keep the economy running despite higher rates, and earnings growth is forecast at 25% for 2026.
tension_points.bear_case: Continued hikes in December and March, waning fiscal support and tighter financial conditions weigh on 2027 growth, prompting the Fed to turn dovish. Valuations are compressing and AI credit stress is building.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slower growth next year is the stated driver of the cut call, so continued above-trend growth into 2027 would undermine the dovish pivot.
